tagline: Your DSA grind, on your GitHub. Automatically.
summary: A browser extension that commits every accepted competitive-programming solution to your own GitHub repository — code, problem statement and an optional AI review — with no extra steps after install. Practice that used to vanish into a judge's servers becomes a reviewable history.
highlights: Commits accepted solutions automatically, so a months-long practice habit shows up as real repository history.
Keeps the commit path and the AI review path separate, so a slow or failing AI provider never delays or blocks a commit.
Batches finished reviews through a ten-minute maintenance alarm into one atomic commit, rather than one commit per review.
Maps the same problem across different judges to a canonical identity, so solving it twice does not create two entries.
Uses your own AI provider key and your own repository — the extension is the plumbing, not the host.

sections.heading: Why the two paths are separate
sections.body: The obvious design runs the AI review and then commits the result. It fails the moment a provider is slow or down: the commit — the part that actually matters — is held hostage by the part that does not. Here the commit goes out immediately on acceptance, the review is queued in IndexedDB, and a maintenance alarm folds completed reviews into a later atomic commit. A dead provider costs you review text, never a commit.
